newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: LEIGHTON YEAR PROFIT SEEN UP 25 PERCENT.
newsitem.headline: LEIGHTON YEAR PROFIT SEEN UP 25 PERCENT.

text.p: Australia's largest construction group, Leighton Holdings Ltd, is expected to report a jump in pre-abnormal net profit of about 25 percent for the year.

Leighton, due to report on Thursday, is estimated to show a pre-abnormal net profit of between A$79.0 million and A$85.4 million for the year to June 30 with a median consensus of A$81.0 million for the 1996/97 year, analysts said.
This compares with a profit of A$65 million a year earlier.
Analysts said the forecast of a record profit was based on record work on hand covering construction, infrastructue projects and contract mining activities in Australia and Asia.
One Melbourne-based analyst forecast a 1996/97 pre-abnormal net profit of A$81 million for Leighton, which is 44.9 percent owned by German construction group Hochtief Ag.

"You can expect a reasonable contribution from contract mining, civil engineering, building as it comes to the end of the (Sydney) casino contract and out of Asia, so it will be across the board," the analyst said.
Another Melbourne-based analyst forecast a pre-abnormal net profit of A$80.9 million, based on a bulging orderbook.
Leighton's work on hand at June 30 was seen at between A$3.5 billion and A$4.0 billion.
Analysts expect the profit growth to continue in the 1997/98 year, but at a slower rate.

"The rate of growth (in 1997/98) will slow but they will still go forward," said ABN AMRO Hoare Govett analyst Fabian Babich, who expects Leighton to report a pre-abnormal net profit of A$82 million in 1996/97.
Analysts forecast Leighton to report a pre-abnormal net profit of about A$90 million in 1997/98, a rise of 11 percent on the 1996/97 profit consensus forecast.
The expected strong profit result for 1996/97 has already been built into Leighton's share price, which has risen 40 percent since the start of the 1996/97 year.
